exact_statement: As recorded in the pinned N51 source package, a coefficient-blind deterministic generator using unary n,B prints a polynomial-size list of n-tuples of integer square matrices whose prime-subfield reductions hit every family of at most B feasible affine pencils of order at most B over every coefficient field. With B=2s+1, the supplied reduction claims a defined invertible hit for each nonzero admissible size-s noncommutative rational formula and preserves every inverse occurrence in its original expression tree.
assumptions: Pencil feasibility means invertibility at some matrix evaluation over a coefficient-field extension.
For the rational-formula corollary, the formula is nonzero and has a nonempty original expression domain.
The source package reports internal proof/audit passes; the full generator was not executed and external correctness/priority are unresolved.
status: source-derived candidate; interface and supplied derivation reconstructed; not externally verified
novelty_boundary: The source-derived integer-list composition is not externally priority-cleared. This task reconstructs its stated interface and does not certify the generator or claim novelty.
costs: The source claims polynomial dense-output bit cost in n,B with impractical constants; it reports more than 4e62 tuples in an underlying n=B=1 example and says the full generator was not executed. Formula coefficient representation, formula evaluation, exact matrix/rank output, and physical acquisition are separate costs.
falsifier: A counterexample to the source theorem within its exact feasible-pencil or admissible-formula interface, or an independently verified construction failure, would refute the claim.
next_gate: External expert verification of the all-characteristic integer-list construction, complete generator execution at a nontrivial instance, and an acquisition/evaluation interface with explicit cost bounds.

exact_statement: Let X1,...,X5 range over strictly positive 2x2 continuous-time Markov transition kernels. The free rational formula Phi=s4(X1,X2,X3,X4)(I+X5)^(-1), where s4 is the degree-4 standard noncommutative polynomial, is nonzero over the free skew field and is defined at every such physical tuple, but Phi evaluates to the zero matrix for every such tuple. Therefore a universal nonzero-formula hit over unrestricted matrix substitutions does not guarantee a nonzero experiment in a fixed two-state pathway control family.
assumptions: The pathway state space is exactly two states and each intervention is represented by its 2x2 transition kernel.
Every pulse has positive rates and positive duration, so the second eigenvalue of each transition kernel lies in (0,1).
Matrix products encode sequential pulse composition.
status: internally reconstructed exact counterexample, conditional only on the stated two-state model
novelty_boundary: The Amitsur-Levitzki identity and two-state receptor models are established prior art. The new work product is the exact application-interface obstruction and its inverse-domain-preserving formula instance, not a new algebraic identity or biological claim.
costs: The physical model has two fitted rates per pulse condition. Estimating each 2x2 kernel requires preparing both starting states and classifying endpoints. The N51 substitution dimensions, arbitrary signed entries, exact formula-evaluation costs, and inverse-gate condition numbers have no physical encoding in the source. The illustrative order-response assay needs about 8,527 independent observations per order for 80% power at 5% under an ideal two-binomial approximation; this ignores overdispersion and misclassification.
falsifier: An exact rational 2x2 tuple with s4(X1,X2,X3,X4) nonzero and det(I+X5) nonzero would falsify the obstruction; the Amitsur-Levitzki theorem rules out such a tuple over commutative fields.
next_gate: For any enlarged pathway with D>2 resolved states, supply a deterministic encoding of an actual N51 hitting tuple into valid rate generators, calibrated positive singular-value margins at every inverse node, a final readout margin, and a frozen held-out comparison with an equally informed direct schedule-search baseline.

exact_statement: For the displayed two-state pulse kernels PA=[[9/10,1/10],[1/5,4/5]] and PB=[[7/10,3/10],[2/5,3/5]], an initial OFF state has active endpoint probability 33/100 for A-then-B and 31/100 for B-then-A.
assumptions: Row-vector state distributions and sequential multiplication p -> p PA PB or p -> p PB PA.
The displayed kernels are calibrated exactly and endpoint state classification is error-free for the ideal sample-size calculation.
status: exact model derivation plus finite rational arithmetic diagnostic; biological realization untested
novelty_boundary: This is an illustrative parameterized model prediction, not an experimentally established sequence effect for any named receptor.
costs: Two reversed sequence arms; approximately 8,527 independent endpoint observations per arm under the ideal normal-approximation 80%-power calculation, before batch, state-preparation, ligand, and measurement costs.
falsifier: In a blinded randomized assay with validated washout and calibrated state readout, the reversed-order difference falls outside the preregistered CTMC prediction interval or reverses sign under repeated independent batches.
next_gate: Acquire one receptor system's pulse-response kinetics, fit alpha and beta from single-pulse data, freeze the two-sequence prediction, and test on held-out randomized AB and BA protocols.
